messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Purview | Information Protection: Auto-labeling support for legacy Microsoft Office file formats
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Purview auto-labeling will support legacy Office files (.doc, .xls, .ppt) in SharePoint and OneDrive starting late November 2026. Existing policies need a minor edit and rerun to apply this. New policies support these formats automatically in both simulation and enforcement modes.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 24, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

Microsoft Purview service-side auto-labeling is adding support for legacy Microsoft Office file formats, including Word (.doc), Excel (.xls), and PowerPoint (.ppt). Organizations can automatically evaluate and apply sensitivity labels to these files in SharePoint and OneDrive. These legacy file formats will be supported in both simulation and enforcement.

Rollout schedule

  • Public Preview: Beginning in late November 2026 (previously early November) and expected to complete by early December 2026 (previously mid-November)
  • General Availability: Beginning in mid-December 2026 (previously late November) and expected to complete by late December 2026 (previously late November)

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Purview service-side auto-labeling policies for files stored in SharePoint and OneDrive

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Purview
  • SharePoint
  • OneDrive
  • Microsoft Word (.doc)
  • Microsoft Excel (.xls)
  • Microsoft PowerPoint (.ppt)

What will happen

  • Service-side auto-labeling will support legacy Word (.doc), Excel (.xls), and PowerPoint (.ppt) files stored in SharePoint and OneDrive.
  • New auto-labeling policies will automatically support these file formats.
  • Existing auto-labeling policies require a small policy edit and another policy run to restart the crawl and evaluate legacy Office files.
  • For example, an admin can add or remove a comment in the policy, save the change, and then run the policy again.
  • These file formats will be supported in both simulation and enforcement.

Action required and recommendations

If you want existing auto-labeling policies to evaluate legacy Office files:

  • Review your sensitivity labels and auto-labeling policies, including the SharePoint and OneDrive locations in scope.
  • Identify the policies for which you want to extend coverage to legacy Office files.
  • Make a small edit to each existing policy, such as adding or removing a policy comment, and save the change.
  • Run the policy again to restart the crawl so that it can evaluate the newly supported file formats.
  • Before enabling a new or updated policy, run it in simulation mode and review the results to confirm that it identifies the intended content.

New policies do not require the additional edit and policy run.

Learn more

  • Auto-labeling policies | Microsoft Purview
  • Automatically apply a sensitivity label to Microsoft 365 data | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. The change expands the files that auto-labeling policies can evaluate and label to include legacy .doc, .xls, and .ppt files in SharePoint and OneDrive, according to the request.
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Admins manage the capability through Microsoft Purview auto-labeling policies. Microsoft Learn identifies the Microsoft Purview portal's Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies surface for service-side auto-labeling.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Purview | Communication Compliance: Policy alerts improvements
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance will enhance policy alert customization, allowing admins to adjust alert frequency and recipients. Public preview starts October 2026, with general availability by mid-August 2027. Features include pseudonymized usernames, role-based access, and audit logs to support compliance and privacy.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 25, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.

Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance is improving the capabilities and customization of policy alerts.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 181825.

When this will happen:

Public Preview: We will begin rolling out October 2026 (previously late July 2025) and expect to complete by end of October 2026 (previously mid-Aug 2025).

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out late May 2027 and expect to complete by mid-August 2027.

How this will affect your organization:

Communication Compliance is improving the capabilities and customization of policy alerts. Admins will be able to customize the alert frequency per policy as well as adjust the email alerts frequency and recipients within the policy creation wizard by navigating to the new alerts page.

This new feature is available by default.

What you need to do to prepare:

Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance provides the tools to help organizations detect business conduct and regulatory compliance violations (e.g. SEC or FINRA), such as sensitive or confidential information, harassing or threatening language, and sharing of adult content. Usernames are pseudonymized by default, role-based access controls are built in, investigators are opted in by an admin, and audit logs are in place to help ensure user-level privacy.

You can access the Communication Compliance solution in the Microsoft Purview compliance portal. 

Learn more: 

• Learn about communication compliance 

• Create and manage communication compliance alert policies | Microsoft Learn

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Purview | DLM: Legacy Teams retention policies that cover Copilot will be treated as Teams-only
messageCenterItems.summary: Starting mid-January 2027, legacy Microsoft Teams retention policies will apply only to Teams data, excluding Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions. Organizations must create separate retention policies for Copilot to maintain compliance. Existing Teams retention behavior remains unchanged, but action is required to cover Copilot data.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 25, 2026: We are updating this post as a reminder. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

Microsoft Purview is updating how legacy Microsoft Teams retention policies are applied. Some existing retention policies that are scoped to Teams currently also apply to Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions. Beginning with this rollout, these legacy policies will be treated as Teams-only policies and will no longer implicitly apply to Copilot workloads.

Rollout schedule

  • Worldwide: Beginning in mid-January 2027 (previously late October 2026) and expected to complete by end of January 2027 (previously mid-November)

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Purview retention policies that were historically configured for Microsoft Teams and currently rely on those policies to retain or delete Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions
  • Compliance administrators and records management administrators responsible for retention policy configuration

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Purview
  • Microsoft Teams
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot

What will happen

  • Legacy Teams retention policies that currently affect both Teams and Copilot data will be treated as Teams-only policies.
  • Copilot interactions will no longer be retained or deleted through these legacy Teams retention policies.
  • Retention behavior for Microsoft Teams content will remain unchanged.
  • Organizations that require retention coverage for Copilot interactions must configure retention settings specifically for the Copilot workload.

Action required and recommendations

Action is required if you currently rely on Teams retention policies to govern Copilot interactions.

  • Review existing Microsoft Purview retention policies to identify policies that may currently apply to Copilot interactions.
  • Determine whether your organization requires retention or deletion controls for Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions.
  • Configure retention policies explicitly for the Copilot workload to maintain the desired compliance coverage after this change.
  • Update internal compliance documentation and administrator guidance as needed.
  • Inform compliance and records management stakeholders of this change.

Compliance considerations

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Copilot interaction data will no longer be governed by legacy Teams retention policies and must be managed through retention policies explicitly configured for the Copilot workload.
Does the change modify, interrupt, or disable retention policies, holds, or deletion workflows?Yes. Existing Teams retention policies that currently affect Copilot interactions will no longer apply to Copilot workloads. Organizations requiring Copilot retention coverage must configure retention policies specifically for Copilot.
